# Solution

## Setup

The surplus function is
$$f(n) = n - \sum_{i=1}^{m}\lfloor r_i n\rfloor = \sum_{i=1}^{m}\{r_i n\},$$
where $\{x\}=x-\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the fractional part. We seek $\max_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}} f(n)$.

## Upper bound

Since $\sum r_i = 1$, we have $\sum r_i n = n$, an integer. Therefore
$$f(n) = \sum_{i=1}^{m}\{r_i n\} = \sum_{i=1}^{m} r_i n - \sum_{i=1}^{m}\lfloor r_i n\rfloor = n - \sum_{i=1}^{m}\lfloor r_i n\rfloor,$$
which is an integer. Each fractional part satisfies $0 \le \{r_i n\} < 1$, so
$$0 \le f(n) < m.$$
Being an integer strictly less than $m$, we conclude
$$f(n) \le m-1 \quad\text{for every } n.$$

## Achieving the bound

Write each $r_i = p_i/q_i$ in lowest terms with $q_i \ge 2$ (since $r_i$ is a positive rational strictly between $0$ and $1$: the $r_i$ are positive and sum to $1$ with $m\ge 2$, so no $r_i$ equals $1$). Let
$$Q = \operatorname{lcm}(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_m),$$
and take $n = Q - 1 > 0$.

For each $i$, $r_i Q = p_i Q/q_i$ is an integer (since $q_i \mid Q$). Hence
$$r_i(Q-1) = r_i Q - r_i = (\text{integer}) - r_i.$$
Since $0 < r_i < 1$, the fractional part of an integer minus $r_i$ is $1 - r_i$:
$$\{r_i(Q-1)\} = 1 - r_i.$$
Therefore
$$f(Q-1) = \sum_{i=1}^{m}(1 - r_i) = m - \sum_{i=1}^{m} r_i = m - 1.$$

## Conclusion

The upper bound $m-1$ is attained at $n = Q-1$, so the maximum possible number of chips in the surplus bin is

$$\boxed{m-1}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
